transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

That is usually a failed door-balance spring or its hinge cable, rather than a door latch fault. Built-in dishwasher doors are counterbalanced so they stay where you leave them; if a cable snaps, comes off, or a spring/hinge fails, the door drops heavily. With the dishwasher switched off, check that no plinth panel, cabinet trim or item in the door area is fouling either hinge, and look only for anything obviously loose or broken at the lower sides. Avoid continuing to let it slam, as it can strain the hinges and door. If nothing is trapped, it will normally need an engineer to refit or replace the balance/hinge parts, which involves removing the integrated door or pulling the machine out.

Nothing seems trapped, the door closes square and latches fine. I did hear a twang last week when it went, and with a torch under the plinth I can see a loose spring hanging on the right side. The left side still has a bit of tension, right side has none.

That is very strong evidence of a right-hand door-balance fault: most likely the spring has come off because its cable or retaining connector has failed, or less commonly the spring itself has broken. The twang and complete loss of tension on that side fit it exactly; the latch is not the problem. With it switched off and isolated, use the torch only—do not pull the spring, as it can be under tension. See whether the hanging spring is whole and has merely come off an attachment point, or whether there is a snapped cable/end fitting nearby. Either result normally needs the machine pulled out and the balance cable/spring assembly or hinge parts refitted or replaced, so an engineer is the sensible route. Keep supporting the door when opening it until repaired.

candidates: Door balance spring or hinge cable has failed or come off (high)
